The '''2026 United States Senate election in Louisiana''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Louisiana]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congresswoman [[Julia Letlow]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Tensas Parish police juror [[Jamie Davis (Lousiana)|Jamie Davis]] are the nominees for their respective parties. The winner will succeed two-term Republican incumbent [[Bill Cassidy]], who was defeated in the primary.

Considered vulnerable to a Republican challenger after he voted to convict President [[Donald Trump]] in [[second impeachment trial of Donald Trump|his second impeachment trial]], Cassidy received 24.8% of the vote in the May 16 primary behind Letlow's 44.8% and state treasurer [[John Fleming (Louisiana politician)|John Fleming]]'s 28.3%.<ref name=CassidyRunning>{{cite news |title=Bill Cassidy discusses reelection plans while blistering Louisiana closed party primary law |last=Hilburn |first=Greg |work=[[The Times (Shreveport, Louisiana)|The Times]] |location=[[Shreveport, Louisiana|Shreveport]] |date=January 30, 2024 |access-date=March 31, 2024 |url=https://www.shreveporttimes.com/story/news/2024/01/30/will-louisiana-senator-bill-cassidy-run-for-reelection-under-new-closed-party-primary-law-he-hates/72405214007/}}</ref> Letlow, endorsed by Trump, advanced to a runoff against Fleming on June 27 and won the nomination with 56.9% of the vote. A Democratic runoff between Davis and political consultant Gary Crockett was held the same day, which Davis won with 79.9% of the vote.

With the enactment of House Bill 17 in 2024, the race is the first U.S. Senate election in Louisiana to utilize party primaries instead of a single [[Nonpartisan blanket primary|blanket primary]] since [[2010 United States Senate election in Louisiana|2010]].<ref name="NoOpenPrimaries"/><ref name="Uphill"/> Democrats have not won a Senate election in Louisiana since [[2008 United States Senate election in Louisiana|2008]].

==Background==

===Change of electoral system===
In January 2024, governor [[Jeff Landry]] signed House Bill 17, sponsored by representative [[Julie Emerson]], which eliminated the top-two [[Louisiana primary]] system in favor of partisan primaries in elections for [[United States Congress|Congress]], the [[Louisiana Board of Elementary and Secondary Education|Board of Elementary and Secondary Education]], the [[Louisiana Public Service Commission|Public Service Commission]], and the [[Louisiana Supreme Court|state's Supreme Court]]. Unaffiliated voters may vote in the primaries, but not members of other parties, including the [[Independent Party of Louisiana]]. The bill also indicated the use of [[two-round system|runoff elections]] if no candidate receives a majority in their respective primary. The law will take effect beginning with the 2026 elections, making this election the first in which Louisiana will elect a U.S. senator using this system since [[2010 United States Senate election in Louisiana|2010]]; the top-two primary was first implemented in congressional elections in [[1978 United States Senate election in Louisiana|1978]].<ref name=NoOpenPrimaries>{{cite news |title=Gov. Landry, lawmakers disrupt how Louisiana has voted for nearly 50 years |last=Muller |first=Wesley |work=[[States Newsroom|Louisiana Illuminator]] |date=January 19, 2024 |access-date=March 31, 2024 |url=https://lailluminator.com/2024/01/19/closed-primaries-2/}}</ref>

===Primary challenge to Cassidy===
Senator [[Bill Cassidy]], who has held this seat since 2015, gained notoriety within the Republican Party for his vocal criticism of [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]. Cassidy denounced the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 U.S. Capitol attack]], accused participants of [[sedition]], and voted to certify the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 election]] results.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Atoms |first1=Greg |title=Senator Bill Cassidy Says Pro-Trump Rioters Committed Sedition |url=https://710keel.com/senator-bill-cassidy-says-pro-trump-rioters-committed-sedition/ |access-date=January 10, 2021 |work=[[KEEL]] |date=January 8, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He was one of seven Senate Republicans who voted to convict Trump for [[incitement]] of [[insurrection]] during [[second impeachment trial of Donald Trump|his second impeachment trial]], prompting the [[Republican Party of Louisiana]] to [[censure]] him.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mena |first1=Kelly |last2=Merica |first2=Dan |title=Louisiana Republican Party censures Cassidy following vote to convict Trump |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/13/politics/bill-cassidy-louisiana-republican-party-censure/index.html |access-date=February 14, 2021 |work=[[CNN]] |date=February 13, 2021}}</ref> During [[Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign|Trump's 2024 campaign]], Cassidy publicly opposed his candidacy, citing Trump's [[indictments against Donald Trump|four criminal indictments]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Republican Bill Cassidy derides Trump and calls 2024 race 'sorry state of affairs' |last=Yang |first=Maya |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=March 17, 2024 |access-date=March 31, 2024 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/mar/17/republican-bill-cassidy-donald-trump-interview}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=GOP Sen. Bill Cassidy says Trump should drop out of the 2024 presidential race|last=Concepcion |first=Summer |work=[[NBC News]] |date=August 20, 2023 |access-date=August 20, 2023|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2024-election/gop-senator-says-trump-drop-2024-presidential-race-rcna100878}}</ref>

Cassidy's stance led analysts to view him as vulnerable to a [[Trumpism|pro-Trump]] [[primary challenge]]. Early speculation in 2024 included Congressman [[Clay Higgins]], a supporter of Trump, who ultimately declined to run.<ref name=Uphill>{{cite news |title=Bill Cassidy faces uphill battle to win reelection but independents can still vote for him |last=Bridges |first=Tyler |work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate]] |date=January 28, 2024 |access-date=March 31, 2024 |url=https://www.nola.com/news/politics/bill-cassidy-faces-uphill-battle-to-win-reelection/article_5e2c6d4c-bca5-11ee-b87d-f3e1204248de.html}}</ref><ref name=":0"/> On January 18, 2026, Trump endorsed Julia Letlow, who officially entered the race two days later.<ref name="Trump/Letlow">{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Meredith Lee |last2=Carney |first2=Jordain |title=Louisiana's Letlow prepares Senate bid after Trump endorsement |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/18/louisianas-letlow-prepares-senate-bid-00735697 |publisher=Politico |access-date=19 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Beaumont |first1=Thomas |last2=Barrow |first2=Bill |title=Rep.
